title: The Legends of Lost Nazi Gold
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and legends of Nazi gold. They begin with Nazi economic desperation (Weimar hyperinflation, lack of natural resources) that drove looting, starting with Austria's central bank and Vienna's Jewish citizens, and the gold shipments Britain sent to Fort Knox (Project Fish) and Russia's evacuation of its gold. They cover the scale of looting, including gold taken from Holocaust victims, and the Merkers mine treasure discovered by US forces in 1945. Next they cover treasure legends: Lake Toplitz in Austria (boxes dumped, counterfeit British pound notes, dangerous layered water and logs), the Amber Room hunt near Deutsche Evern/Deutsche Catherinenburg (the hosts say Deutsche Catherinenburg), the Owl Mountains ghost train and the Riese tunnel project in Poland, and the wreck of the S S Minden off Iceland, sunk in 1939 and searched for in 2017. They then discuss postwar restitution through the Tripartite Gold Commission, Switzerland's laundering of Nazi gold, and a 2019 accusation that Venezuela's Maduro government trafficked in suspected Nazi gold. The episode closes with a listener mail correction about a cited source (Charles Murray) and a brief note on a show called Monuments Men, plus sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Curly's Gold tangent
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Jack Palance, Clint Eastwood, and the Legend of Curly's Gold, then set up the episode's theme of Nazi thieves.

segments.title: Why the Nazis needed to steal gold
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Germany lacked resources and money to fund the war, citing Weimar-era hyperinflation and the worthless Reichsmark. Gold was a universally accepted commodity, and neutral countries would not accept Reichsmarks.

segments.title: Looting of Austria and gold shipments
segments.summary: Nazis looted gold from Vienna's Jewish citizens and Austria's central bank, then seized Austrian gold sent to England. The hosts describe Project Fish, Britain's gold sent to Fort Knox, and Russia's evacuation of its gold to the Urals.

segments.title: Scale of Nazi gold theft and tooth gold
segments.summary: The hosts total the gold stolen from occupied countries and from individuals, including dental fillings, wedding rings, and jewelry from concentration camp victims. Most looted gold went to the Reichsbank before being moved to secret locations as bombing raids hit Berlin.

segments.title: Merkers mine treasure
segments.summary: US military police heard about gold stored in a potash mine near Merkers. The army found the Merkers mine treasure, valued at about 238 million dollars, which was about half of the gold unaccounted for.

segments.title: Chuck and Josh's pie and Rush banter
segments.summary: Off-topic banter about favorite pies, cherry pie, the Warrant song, Sebastian Bach of Skid Row, and Rush.

segments.title: Lake Toplitz legend
segments.summary: Nazis reportedly dumped boxes into Lake Toplitz in the Austrian Alps near the war's end. Contents are debated, possibly gold, documents, artwork, or morphine. Counterfeit British pounds were recovered in 1959 and 1983, and the lake has dangerous layered water and logs that hamper diving.

segments.title: Amber Room and Deutsche Catherinenburg
segments.summary: The Amber Room, a gift from Prussian King Frederick William I to Peter the Great, disappeared during World War II after being displayed in Königsberg. Treasure hunters searched near Deutsche Catherinenburg using a father's notes and radar, but their partnership ended in acrimony in 2008 with no known result.

segments.title: Owl Mountains ghost train and Riese tunnels
segments.summary: A legend says a Nazi ghost train full of loot was driven into a tunnel in Poland's Owl Mountains. Real tunnels were dug between 1943 and 1945 in the Riese project, built by concentration camp forced labor. The Soviets arrived and the Nazis blew up the tunnels. The Hungarian Gold Train was a real intercepted train.

segments.title: S S Minden shipwreck off Iceland
segments.summary: The German merchant ship S S Minden, reportedly carrying resin, was disabled by the British Royal Navy off Iceland in 1939 and scuttled by its captain in about 70 feet of water. In 2017 a salvage team chartered a ship and reportedly located the wreck, claiming it sought gold.

segments.title: Tripartite Gold Commission and Swiss gold
segments.summary: Postwar Allied commission tried to return gold to central banks and Holocaust survivors. Switzerland was revealed to have laundered Nazi gold and reportedly still holds some of it.

segments.title: Venezuela and Nazi gold in the modern gold trade
segments.summary: In 2019 the Simon Wiesenthal Center accused Venezuela's Maduro administration of trafficking suspected Nazi gold, about 77 tons, which it said may have funded a Fourth Reich effort.

segments.title: Listener mail correction and Monuments Men
segments.summary: A listener pointed out that an earlier episode cited Charles Murray, whose work has been used by white supremacists. The hosts apologize. They also clarify Monuments Men versus Museum Men.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing reminder to contact the show.
